options: Telling the customer, to give them a chance to explain
Sending the SAR to the customer's accountant
Sharing the underlying facts with another financial institution to prepare a joint SAR
Mentioning the SAR in a public court filing for a debt claim, because court filings are protected by litigation privilege
quiz.explanation: The rule allows disclosure of a SAR to FinCEN, law enforcement and BSA examiners, and of the underlying facts to another institution for a joint SAR. Disclosure to the customer or third parties is prohibited.

quiz.question: A customer sends a USD 4,000 wire from Bramblecove. Which BSA rule requires Bramblecove, as the originator's bank, to record the originator's name and address, the amount and the beneficiary's bank?
options: The funds transfer recordkeeping rule for transfers of USD 3,000 or more
The CTR rule
The SAR rule
The OFAC reporting rule
quiz.explanation: 31 CFR 1020.410(a) requires records for funds transfers of USD 3,000 or more, including originator name and address, amount, execution date, payment instructions and the beneficiary's bank.

quiz.question: How long must Bramblecove keep a copy of a filed SAR and its supporting documentation?
options: Five years after the account closes
Five years from the date of filing
Ten years from the transaction
Until law enforcement confirms receipt
quiz.explanation: The SAR rule requires a copy of each SAR and its supporting documents to be kept for five years from filing; the documents are treated as filed with the SAR.

quiz.question: USAA Federal Savings Bank's 2022 FinCEN penalty followed which kind of failure?
options: Opening accounts for foreign shell banks
Processing payments through blocked Russian banks because its sanctions filter was updated late after new designations
Failing to verify beneficial owners of trusts
Willful failure to timely and accurately file thousands of SARs, with large alert backlogs
quiz.explanation: FinCEN found at least 3,873 SARs were not timely and accurately filed and that alert and case backlogs had grown to around 90,000 alerts and 6,900 cases, linked to understaffing.

sessions.title: OFAC Sanctions, Testing, Training, Enforcement and the Proposed Rule
sessions.summary: Handle OFAC matches, support independent testing, the BSA officer and training, learn from enforcement actions, and understand the April 2026 proposed AML/CFT program rule.
objectives: Apply OFAC blocking, rejecting, reporting and recordkeeping duties under strict liability
Describe the five components of OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments
Explain what examiners expect of independent testing, the BSA officer and training
Describe the April 2026 proposed AML/CFT program rule and its status

cards.title: 10:40 pm: a designation lands
cards.setting: Sanctions operations, Columbus, late evening. The exam starts on Monday.

lines.text: OFAC just designated eight companies and two banks. Our filter vendor updates tomorrow morning. There are wires queued for 6 am.
One queued wire routes through a bank on tonight's list as the intermediary.
And our 'auto-close repeat alert' rule would release that wire if an analyst cleared the same name last month.
Then we load the new names manually tonight and switch that suppression rule off for blocked banks. OFAC liability doesn't wait for vendor schedules.
Stage five, the Examiner's Table: sanctions, testing, the BSA officer, training, enforcement and the rule FinCEN has proposed. Last stage before the final boss.

scenes.heading: Strict liability
scenes.narration: OFAC may impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis. In many cases a US person can be liable even without knowing, or having reason to know, that the activity was prohibited.

scenes.heading: Block or reject
scenes.narration: Funds in which a blocked person has an interest are blocked and placed in a segregated, interest-bearing account. Where a program prohibits a transaction but does not require blocking, the bank rejects it instead.

scenes.heading: Report within ten business days
scenes.narration: Both blocked and rejected transactions are reported to OFAC through the OFAC Reporting System within 10 business days.

scenes.heading: Keep records for ten years
scenes.narration: Records of transactions subject to OFAC rules are kept for 10 years, and for blocked property 10 years after it is unblocked.

scenes.heading: Five components
scenes.narration: OFAC's 2019 Framework for Compliance Commitments names five components of a sanctions compliance program: management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, and training.

cards.title: OFAC's five compliance components
cards.caption: From A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments (2019). OFAC may weigh an effective program when deciding penalties.

items.label: Management commitment
items.detail: Approves the program, gives it authority, resources and a culture of compliance

items.label: Risk assessment
items.detail: Customers, products, geographies and counterparties assessed for sanctions risk

items.label: Internal controls
items.detail: Screening, escalation, list updates, blocking and reporting procedures

items.label: Testing and auditing
items.detail: Independent checks, with fixes for root causes of any weakness

items.label: Training
items.detail: Periodic and at least annual, job-specific, with assessments

cards.question: A Bramblecove wire to a newly designated company went out two hours after the designation, before the filter was updated. Nobody knew. What does OFAC's strict liability standard mean here?
options: No violation is possible because nobody knew
The bank may still face civil liability, though OFAC weighs all facts and the bank's compliance program
Only the employee who released the wire is liable
Liability applies only if the bank profited
cards.explanation: Under strict liability, OFAC may hold a US person civilly liable even without knowledge or reason to know. OFAC then considers the totality of facts, including an effective risk-based program and remediation, when choosing its response.

cards.title: Block, reject or process?
cards.prompt: Sort each payment by the right sanctions action, based only on the facts given.

items.text: A wire to an account owned by a company on the SDN List
A wire routed through an intermediary bank that OFAC has just blocked
A payment prohibited by a sanctions program that has no blocked person's interest in it
A screening hit on a common name, cleared with documented date-of-birth and address mismatches
A domestic payroll payment with no sanctions nexus and no alert

cards.title: Real case: Bank of America and OFAC, 2026
cards.body:
On **13 October 2026 OFAC** announced that **Bank of America, N.A.** agreed to pay **USD 11,662,930** to settle **475 apparent violations** of several sanctions programs, including Russia, Belarus, Iran, narcotics and global terrorism.

OFAC described four issues, including:

- a third-party **routing directory** that still contained **blocked banks**, so payments went through them
- payments processed **before the screening filter was updated** after new designations
- payments released by an **alert suppression rule** that auto-cleared alerts resembling past false positives
- **human error** in clearing true matches and in handling accounts linked to blocked persons

OFAC found the violations **non-egregious** but largely **not voluntarily self-disclosed**, and gave **no reduction** for remediation or cooperation.

**Lesson:** list updates, suppression logic and vendor data are controls, and OFAC tests them.

Source: OFAC enforcement release, 13 October 2026 (ofac.treasury.gov).

cards.title: Independent testing and the BSA officer
cards.body:
**Independent testing** checks whether the program is designed well and works in practice. The rules let the bank use its **own personnel or an outside party**, but testers must be independent of the BSA function they test. Findings go to senior management and the board, and the bank fixes **root causes**, not just individual files.

**The BSA officer** is the individual designated to **coordinate and monitor day-to-day compliance**. Examiners look at whether this person has the **authority, independence, expertise and resources** to do the job, and reports directly enough to senior management and the board to raise problems.

OFAC's framework notes that a bank may have **one person** oversee both BSA and sanctions compliance, depending on its size and complexity.

**Training** must reach appropriate personnel, matched to their roles, including directors, and be updated when rules change, with records kept.

cards.title: What an examiner asks, and who answers
cards.prompt: Match each examiner question to the pillar or role that should answer it.

pairs.right: Who coordinates day-to-day compliance, and do they have the authority and staff to do it?
Who tested the alert scenarios last year, and were they independent of the team that runs them?
What did tellers, wire staff and the board each learn this year, and how do you know they understood it?
How are new OFAC designations loaded into screening the same day?
When did the board approve the program, and what reports has it received since?

cards.title: The training plan
cards.setting: Dana's office, Friday afternoon. The board's risk committee meets on Tuesday.

lines.text: Can't we buy a 20-minute annual video for everyone and call training done?
A shared foundation is fine. But tellers need cash and structuring, Elena's team needs CIP, your desk needs correspondent EDD, and Amina's analysts need screening.
And OFAC's framework expects training at least annually, job-specific, with assessments that hold people accountable.
Remember the bank that put staff from other departments into alert review with no AML training? The examiners did.

cards.title: Real case: Shinhan Bank America, 2023
cards.body:
In **September 2023 FinCEN** imposed a **USD 15 million** civil money penalty on **Shinhan Bank America**, crediting a **USD 5 million** FDIC penalty. The bank admitted willful violations of the BSA.

FinCEN described an under-resourced program:

- the bank did not hire enough compliance staff, which caused overload and **high turnover**
- it filled compliance roles with employees from other parts of the bank who had **no prior BSA or AML experience**
- **eight months** after a new monitoring system went live, compliance staff had **not been trained on it**
- some analysts lacked the training to reach well-supported alert decisions
- the bank **struggled to retain a BSA officer**

**Lesson:** the training and BSA officer pillars are tested by results. Untrained people working alerts is a program failure, not a staffing detail.

Source: FinCEN enforcement action 2023-03 (fincen.gov).

cards.title: Designing next year's BSA/AML training
cards.situation: Dana asks you to propose Bramblecove's training plan for next year. Budget is limited. The board wants evidence it works, and the OCC will review training records.

choices.text: One generic 20-minute annual video for everyone, with completion tracked
choices.outcome: Easy to evidence, but it does not match content to roles or test understanding. Examiners and OFAC's framework expect tailoring and assessment.

choices.text: A shared foundation for all staff plus role modules for tellers, onboarding, wires, correspondent and sanctions teams and the board, with assessments, updates for rule changes and complete records
choices.outcome: Best answer. It reaches appropriate personnel, fits each role, includes directors, tests understanding and leaves the records examiners ask for.

choices.text: Train only the BSA/AML department in depth, since they file the SARs
choices.outcome: Front-line staff spot and escalate most unusual activity. Leaving them out weakens the program at its first line.

choices.text: Role modules for front-line teams only, without records of who attended
choices.outcome: Partly right on content, but without records the bank cannot show the pillar works, and the board is left out.

cards.title: Today's rule versus the April 2026 PROPOSAL
cards.caption: The proposal was not final as of November 2026. Follow the current rules until a final rule takes effect.

items.label: Name
items.left: Anti-money laundering (AML) program
items.right: AML/CFT program

items.label: Risk assessment
items.left: Expected by examiners; not required uniformly in the rule text
items.right: Required risk assessment processes, reviewing the government's AML/CFT Priorities

items.label: Pillars
items.left: Internal controls, independent testing, BSA officer, training, plus ongoing CDD
items.right: Four pillars, with ongoing CDD moved under internal controls

items.label: Officer
items.left: A designated individual for day-to-day compliance
items.right: An AML/CFT officer located in the United States

items.label: Training
items.left: Training for appropriate personnel
items.right: Ongoing employee training program, tailored to risk and roles

items.label: Supervision
items.left: Agencies examine and enforce under their powers
items.right: Establish vs maintain test; 30 days' notice to FinCEN before significant supervisory actions

cards.title: The proposed rule: what to know

cards.front: Is the April 2026 AML/CFT program rule in force?
cards.back: No. It is a proposal. Comments closed on 9 June 2026, and no final rule had been issued as of November 2026.

cards.front: What did it replace?
cards.back: It fully superseded FinCEN's July 2024 proposal, which FinCEN withdrew.

cards.front: Establish versus maintain?
cards.back: Design gaps (establishing the program) would be separated from failures to run it in practice (maintaining it), to focus action on significant or systemic failures.

cards.front: Would training survive?
cards.back: Yes. An ongoing employee training program stays one of four pillars, with frequency and content tailored to the bank's risk and staff roles.

cards.front: Do the bank regulators follow?
cards.back: The OCC, FDIC, NCUA and Federal Reserve said they would issue their own aligned proposals for the institutions they supervise.

cards.title: From OFAC match to report
cards.prompt: Put Amina's steps for a confirmed sanctions match on an incoming wire in order.
steps: Stop the payment in the queue before release
Confirm the match against the SDN List details, not just the name
Determine whether the program requires blocking or rejection
Block the funds into a segregated interest-bearing account, or reject the payment
Report the blocked or rejected transaction through the OFAC Reporting System within 10 business days
Keep the records for 10 years and review the root cause of the alert

cards.question: Kevin reads a news story and says, 'FinCEN changed the rules in April, so we now need a US-based AML/CFT officer and a new risk assessment process.' What is the accurate response?
options: He is right; the April 2026 rule took effect immediately
Those are features of a proposed rule that was not final as of November 2026; current rules still apply
The proposal was withdrawn in June 2026
The proposal applies only to the Federal Reserve's banks
cards.explanation: The April 2026 rule is a proposal: comments closed in June 2026 and no final rule had been issued by November 2026. Banks must follow the current program rules while monitoring for a final rule.

cards.question: According to OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments, how often should sanctions training be provided to appropriate employees?
options: Only at induction
On a periodic basis and at a minimum annually
Every three years
Only when OFAC issues new designations
cards.explanation: The framework expects periodic training, at a minimum annually, that gives job-specific knowledge, communicates each employee's responsibilities and holds employees accountable through assessments.

cards.title: Examiner's Table ready
items: OFAC: strict liability; block or reject; report within 10 business days; keep records 10 years.
OFAC's framework: management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, at least annual training.
Independent testing must be independent of the BSA function; the BSA officer needs authority, expertise and resources.
Training should be role-based, include directors, test understanding and leave records.
The April 2026 AML/CFT program rule is a PROPOSAL; current rules apply until a final rule takes effect.

cards.prompt: If an OCC examiner sat at your desk tomorrow and asked you to walk through one BSA or sanctions task you do, what would you show, and which step would you most want to tighten first?

quiz.question: What does OFAC mean when it says civil penalties may be imposed on a strict liability basis?
options: Only intentional violations can be penalised
A US person may be liable even without knowing, or having reason to know, the activity was prohibited
Only the board can be penalised
Penalties can apply only after a criminal court has convicted the bank of knowingly breaching a sanctions program
quiz.explanation: OFAC's introduction to its work explains that in many cases a US person can be civilly liable without knowledge or reason to know. OFAC still considers all facts and circumstances.

quiz.question: Within what time must a bank report a blocked or rejected transaction to OFAC?
options: Within 10 business days, through the OFAC Reporting System
Within 30 calendar days, through FinCEN
Within 15 days, with the CTR
Within 24 hours, by telephone
quiz.explanation: OFAC's FAQs say blocked and rejected transactions are reported through the OFAC Reporting System within 10 business days under 31 CFR 501.603 and 501.604.

quiz.question: A payment is prohibited under a sanctions program, but no blocked person has an interest in it. What should the bank generally do?
options: Block the funds in a segregated account
Process it, since no blocked person is involved
File a SAR instead of any OFAC report
Reject the payment and report the rejection to OFAC
quiz.explanation: Where a program prohibits a transaction but there is no blockable interest, the bank rejects it rather than blocks it, and reports the rejected transaction to OFAC.

quiz.question: How long must a bank keep records of transactions subject to OFAC regulations?
options: Five years from the transaction
Three years after the account closes
Ten years, and for blocked property ten years after it is unblocked
Until OFAC confirms the report
quiz.explanation: OFAC requires records to be kept for 10 years after the transaction or, for blocked property, 10 years after it is unblocked. Note the difference from the five-year BSA period.

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the five essential components in OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments?
options: Management commitment
Customer profitability review
Annual FinCEN certification
External legal opinion on each payment
quiz.explanation: The five components are management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, and training.

quiz.question: Amina's team uses a rule that auto-closes an alert if an analyst cleared an alert on the same criteria before. After a new designation, what does the Bank of America case suggest?
options: Suppression rules are always prohibited
Suppression rules matter only for BSA, not OFAC
Suppression rules are fine without further review if a reputable vendor designed them and the bank has used them for years
Suppression rules must be reviewed so they cannot release payments involving newly blocked parties
quiz.explanation: OFAC's 2026 settlement with Bank of America described payments released by an alert suppression rule that auto-cleared alerts resembling past false positives. Such logic must be controlled and tested.

quiz.question: In the 2023 Shinhan Bank America case, which finding relates most directly to the training pillar?
options: The bank processed payments for blocked banks
The bank kept correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks and failed to obtain certifications from respondents
Compliance staff had not been trained on a new monitoring system eight months after it went live
The bank failed to file CTRs for cash deposits
quiz.explanation: FinCEN found that eight months after implementing a new monitoring system, compliance staff had not been trained on it, and that some analysts lacked the training to make well-supported alert decisions.

quiz.question: What is the status of FinCEN's April 2026 AML/CFT program rule as of November 2026?
options: A final rule in force since April 2026
A proposed rule whose comment period closed in June 2026; it is not yet final
A withdrawn proposal replaced by the 2024 rule
Guidance with no rulemaking
quiz.explanation: FinCEN issued the proposal in April 2026, with comments due by 9 June 2026. It superseded the withdrawn 2024 proposal. No final rule had been issued as of November 2026.

quiz.question: Under the April 2026 proposal, which change would apply to the compliance officer?
options: The officer would have to be a board member
The officer role would be abolished
The AML/CFT officer would have to be located in the United States
The officer would need FinCEN approval before appointment
quiz.explanation: The proposal would require a designated AML/CFT officer located in the United States and accessible to FinCEN and regulators, though staff abroad could still perform some functions. It is not yet final.

quiz.question: Dana must choose a training approach for next year. Which best matches the BSA rules, OFAC's framework and the lessons of enforcement cases?
options: Role-based training for staff and directors, at least annually for sanctions, with assessments and records
A single generic video for all staff each year, with completion tracked but no assessment or role-specific content
Training only for the BSA department
Training only when a regulator finds a problem
quiz.explanation: The program rules require training for appropriate personnel; OFAC expects at least annual, job-specific training with assessments; and cases like Shinhan show untrained staff are a program failure.

references.note: No correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks, reasonable steps against indirect use, owner and agent records, certification at least every three years.

references.title: 31 CFR 1020.320 Reports by banks of suspicious transactions (Federal Reserve Regulatory Service copy)
references.note: USD 5,000 threshold, 30-day deadline (60 if no suspect), five-year retention, SAR confidentiality and safe harbor.

references.title: 31 CFR 1010.311 Filing obligations for reports of transactions in currency (Federal Reserve Regulatory Service copy)
references.note: CTR for currency transactions of more than USD 10,000, aggregated per person per business day, filed within 15 days with five-year retention.

references.title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
references.note: Five components of a sanctions compliance program; training periodic and at least annual, job-specific, with assessments.

references.title: Introduction to the Office of Foreign Assets Control
references.note: Explains strict liability for civil penalties, reporting of blocked and rejected transactions and the ten-year recordkeeping period.

bank.question: An OCC examiner finds that Bramblecove's written BSA program was last approved by the board four years ago, even though new products and an alert-tuning project have changed it since. Which concern is best founded?
options: There is no concern, because board approval is needed only once, when the program is first adopted after the bank is chartered
The program must be approved by FinCEN after each change
The board-approved program no longer reflects how the bank actually manages BSA risk, weakening board oversight
Only the FFIEC can approve changes to a bank's program
bank.explanation: The program must be written and board-approved, and it should reflect current risks and controls. A stale approval means the board is overseeing a program that no longer matches reality. FinCEN does not pre-approve bank programs.

bank.question: A state non-member bank's compliance head says only FinCEN's 31 CFR 1020.210 applies to it. What has she missed?
options: The FDIC's own BSA compliance rule, 12 CFR 326.8, which FinCEN's rule requires the bank to follow
The Federal Reserve's 12 CFR 208.63, which applies to every insured bank regardless of its charter or membership
The OCC's rule, which covers all insured banks
Nothing; FinCEN's rule replaces agency rules
bank.explanation: FinCEN's bank program rule says the bank must also comply with its federal functional regulator's program rule. For a state non-member bank that is the FDIC's 12 CFR 326.8.

bank.question: A bank designates a BSA officer but gives her no staff, no access to the board and requires all SAR decisions to be approved by the head of sales. Which pillar is most clearly undermined?
options: Customer identification
Currency transaction reporting
Independent testing
The designated individual responsible for coordinating and monitoring day-to-day compliance
bank.explanation: A BSA officer exists to coordinate and monitor day-to-day compliance. Without resources, access or independence from business pressure, the designation is a formality and the pillar fails.

bank.question: Which statement about independent testing under the current bank program rules is correct?
options: It must be performed every year by an external accounting firm that also audits the bank's annual financial statements
It may be performed by bank personnel or an outside party, provided the testers are independent of the function
It is performed by the bank's examiners on the bank's behalf
It is optional for banks under a certain size
bank.explanation: The rules allow testing by bank personnel or an outside party. They do not prescribe an external firm or a fixed frequency in the rule text; independence from the BSA function is the key test.

bank.question: Bramblecove's business line wants to reduce monitoring alerts. Which approach is most defensible to examiners?
options: Set a daily ceiling on alerts equal to analyst capacity
Tune scenarios using documented analysis of risk and alert outcomes, with independent validation and approval
Turn off the scenarios that rarely lead to SARs, since low conversion rates prove they add no value, without further analysis
Raise all thresholds by the same percentage to cut volume
bank.explanation: Tuning based on documented, tested risk analysis is acceptable. Capping alerts to match capacity, or cutting scenarios without analysis, lets staffing rather than risk drive monitoring, the failure FinCEN penalised in the U.S. Bank matter.

bank.question: Which body's publication do examiners use to plan and conduct BSA/AML examinations across the federal banking agencies?
options: OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments
FinCEN's SAR Electronic Filing Instructions
The Federal Reserve Regulatory Service
The FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual
bank.explanation: The FFIEC manual is the interagency guide examiners use. OFAC's framework is sanctions guidance, and the Federal Reserve Regulatory Service is a publication of regulations, not an exam manual.

bank.question: FinCEN imposes a penalty on a former chief compliance officer personally. What does this tell bank staff about BSA accountability?
options: Individuals who oversee a BSA program can be held responsible for program failures, not only the bank
Only banks can be penalised under the BSA
Personal penalties apply only to criminal fraud
Only board members can face personal BSA penalties, because they approve the program; compliance staff cannot
bank.explanation: In 2020 FinCEN assessed a USD 450,000 penalty against Michael LaFontaine for his role in U.S. Bank's BSA failures, showing personal accountability for those overseeing compliance.

bank.question: A national bank's BSA examination is conducted by the OCC, but the BSA rules are FinCEN's. Which statement best explains the relationship?
options: The OCC enforces only its own Title 12 safety and soundness rules and has no role at all in examining compliance with the BSA
FinCEN examines national banks directly each year
The OCC examines under authority delegated by FinCEN and its own powers; FinCEN keeps overall BSA enforcement authority
The FFIEC delegates BSA authority to the OCC
bank.explanation: FinCEN has overall authority for BSA enforcement and compliance and delegates examination authority to the federal banking agencies, which also have separate Title 12 powers. This is described in FinCEN's consent orders.

bank.question: A legal entity customer certifies: Ms. Park 25%, Mr. Osei 24%, an SEC-registered listed company 51%, and a CEO with no ownership. The listed company is an excluded entity under the rule. Whom must the bank identify?
options: Ms. Park, Mr. Osei and the CEO
The listed company's directors and the CEO
Only the CEO, because the largest owner is excluded
Ms. Park and the CEO
bank.explanation: Ms. Park meets the 25% threshold; Mr. Osei does not. Where an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual need be identified for that stake. One control person, the CEO, is always required.

bank.question: A nonprofit corporation registered with its state opens an account. Which beneficial ownership requirement applies?
options: Both prongs, like any LLC
Only the control prong: one individual who controls, manages or directs it
Neither prong, because nonprofit corporations are fully excluded from the definition of legal entity customer
Only the ownership prong
bank.explanation: The rule makes nonprofit corporations that have filed with the appropriate state authority subject only to the control prong, because they have no equity owners in the usual sense.

bank.question: Bramblecove wants to rely on an affiliated broker-dealer's CIP for a shared customer. Which condition is required?
options: The affiliate verbally confirms it ran CIP
The customer signs a waiver of CIP
Reliance is reasonable, the affiliate is subject to an AML program rule and a federal functional regulator, and it certifies annually by contract
FinCEN pre-approves the reliance
bank.explanation: The CIP rule permits reliance when it is reasonable, the other institution is subject to a BSA program rule and regulated by a federal functional regulator, and it contracts to certify annually that it performs the specified CIP steps.

bank.question: A customer gives Bramblecove an address and ID number, but non-documentary checks show his date of birth does not match any public record. What should the CIP's failed-verification procedures address?
options: When not to open, the terms of use while verifying, when to close after failed attempts, and when to file a SAR
Only when to file a CTR
Automatic account closure without review
Allowing full use of the account indefinitely while verification continues, as long as the opening deposit is relatively small
bank.explanation: The CIP must include procedures for when the bank cannot form a reasonable belief it knows the customer's identity, covering refusal, interim terms, closure and SAR filing.

bank.question: Bramblecove's CIP list check found no match at opening, but a federal directive later requires an earlier check for a certain list. What applies?
options: The bank checks within a reasonable period after opening, or earlier where another federal law, regulation or directive requires it
The bank checks only at the annual review
The bank never rechecks after opening
The bank checks only if the customer is foreign
bank.explanation: The CIP rule requires the list comparison within a reasonable period after opening, or earlier if required by another federal law, regulation or directive, and the bank must follow directives issued with the lists.

bank.question: An existing legal entity customer, verified in 2024, opens a second account in 2026. Nothing about its ownership or risk has changed. What does FinCEN's February 2026 relief generally permit?
options: Skipping all further customer due diligence on the customer from now on, including monitoring and risk profile updates
Removing the customer's beneficial owner records
Not re-identifying and re-verifying the beneficial owners for the new account, unless risk calls for it
Relying on FinCEN's BOI registry instead
bank.explanation: The exceptive relief means banks generally need not repeat identification and verification of beneficial owners at each new account for existing customers, subject to risk-based exceptions. Ongoing CDD and records remain.

bank.question: A KYC analyst wants to keep beneficial ownership verification records only until the account closes. What does the rule require?
options: All records are kept until the account closes
Verification records are kept five years after the record is made, and identification records five years after the account closes
All records are kept for ten years
Only the certification needs to be kept
bank.explanation: 31 CFR 1010.230(i) sets two retention periods: identification information, including the certification, five years after closure; verification descriptions and discrepancy resolution five years after the record is made.

bank.question: A small business's activity jumps from local card sales to large international wires. Its risk profile says 'local retail'. Which duty is most directly engaged?
options: The Customer Identification Program, which must be repeated in full whenever a customer's account activity changes significantly
The shell bank prohibition
The CTR exemption rules
Risk-based ongoing CDD: monitor for suspicious activity and update customer information, including the risk profile
bank.explanation: Ongoing CDD requires understanding the relationship's nature and purpose, monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions, and updating customer information on a risk basis. A large mismatch should trigger review and possibly a SAR.

bank.question: Which customer is a 'legal entity customer' under the CDD rule?
options: An individual sole proprietor
A bank regulated by a federal functional regulator
A general partnership opening a business account
An issuer with securities registered with the SEC
bank.explanation: The definition covers corporations, LLCs and other entities formed by a public filing, general partnerships and similar foreign entities. Regulated banks and SEC-registered issuers are excluded; sole proprietors are individuals.

bank.question: A foreign bank holds a license from a country Treasury has designated as warranting special measures for money laundering concerns. It is publicly traded. Which EDD step does NOT apply?
options: Identifying each 10% owner of the foreign bank
Enhanced scrutiny of the account, including its AML program
Monitoring transactions through the account
Finding out whether other foreign banks use the account
bank.explanation: The owner identification step applies to foreign banks whose shares are not publicly traded. The other EDD steps apply to any correspondent account for a foreign bank in an EDD category.

bank.question: A foreign respondent offers its own customers direct access to its US dollar account at Bramblecove through subaccounts. What is this, and what does EDD require?
options: A nested account; no extra steps are required
A private banking account; 1010.620 applies instead
A shell bank account; it must be closed
A payable-through account; EDD includes obtaining information on who can direct transactions and the sources and beneficial owners of funds
bank.explanation: A payable-through account lets the foreign bank's customers carry out US banking activity directly. For such accounts in EDD categories, the bank obtains information on those with authority to direct transactions and on the sources and beneficial owners of funds.

bank.question: Bramblecove cannot obtain the information it needs for enhanced due diligence on a correspondent account. What must its procedures address?
options: Only when to inform the customer of the gap
When to refuse to open the account, suspend activity, file a SAR or close the account
When to transfer the account to an affiliate
How to waive EDD with board approval
bank.explanation: Both 1010.610(d) and 1010.620(d) require procedures for when due diligence cannot be performed, including refusal, suspension, SAR filing and closure.

bank.question: Which arrangement is consistent with the shell bank rule?
options: Keeping an account for a foreign bank with no physical presence anywhere, provided it certifies it has a good AML program
Providing a correspondent account to a foreign bank's regulated affiliate that lacks its own physical presence
Ignoring evidence that a respondent passes services to a shell bank
Accepting a shell bank certification that is six years old
bank.explanation: The rule does not prohibit services to a regulated affiliate. It bans accounts for foreign shell banks, requires reasonable steps against indirect use, and the safe harbor needs certification at least every three years.

bank.question: A foreign respondent's 2025 certification lists its US agent for legal process. Bramblecove learns in 2026 that the agent has died. What should it do?
options: Wait for the 2028 recertification
Close the account without contacting the bank
Report the bank to OFAC
Ask the foreign bank to verify or correct the information, or take other steps to obtain correct information
bank.explanation: The interim verification duty applies whenever the bank knows or suspects certified information is no longer correct. Waiting for recertification would lose the safe harbor.

bank.question: A private banking client is a company formed for the benefit of a serving foreign defence minister's brother. Is this within the senior foreign political figure definition for 1010.620?
options: Yes; the definition includes immediate family members and entities formed for their benefit
No; only the official personally is covered
No; relatives and companies are covered only if they themselves hold a senior office in the foreign government
Only if the company is listed on an exchange
bank.explanation: FinCEN's definition of a senior foreign political figure includes the official, entities formed by or for the benefit of such an individual, immediate family members and widely known close associates.

bank.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of enhanced scrutiny for senior foreign political figures under 1010.620(c)?
options: To prevent foreign officials and their families from holding or controlling any private banking account in the US
To report every transaction to the State Department
To detect and report transactions that may involve proceeds of foreign corruption
To apply OFAC blocking to all foreign officials
bank.explanation: The enhanced scrutiny is designed to detect and report transactions that may involve proceeds of foreign corruption, such as embezzled public funds or bribes. It does not ban accounts or replace sanctions screening.

bank.question: A correspondent account was approved for trade payments for a mid-sized foreign bank. Two years later, most flows are round-sum transfers to newly formed companies. Which control should have caught this?
options: The CIP list check at account opening
The shell bank certification
The CTR aggregation rule
Periodic review of account activity against the stated type, purpose and anticipated activity
bank.explanation: 1010.610(a)(3) requires risk-based controls including a periodic review of correspondent account activity to check consistency with the information obtained about the account's type, purpose and expected activity.

bank.question: On 3 May Marcus identifies the facts behind a suspicious wire pattern but cannot identify who controls the receiving accounts. On 20 June he identifies the suspect. What is the latest compliant filing date?
options: 20 July, 30 days after identifying the suspect
2 July, 60 calendar days after initial detection
2 June, 30 days after detection, regardless of the suspect
1 August, 90 days after detection
bank.explanation: With no suspect at detection, the bank may delay up to an additional 30 days, but reporting may not be delayed beyond 60 calendar days after initial detection. 3 May plus 60 days is 2 July.

bank.question: An ongoing money laundering scheme is moving funds through Bramblecove accounts today. Besides filing a SAR on time, what does the SAR rule expect?
options: Freezing all the accounts under OFAC rules
Telling the customers to stop
Immediate notification by telephone to an appropriate law enforcement authority
Waiting for FinCEN to call the bank
bank.explanation: For violations requiring immediate attention, such as ongoing money laundering schemes, the bank must immediately notify an appropriate law enforcement authority by telephone in addition to filing a timely SAR.

bank.question: A teller notices a customer deposited USD 9,900 in cash on Friday night after closing and USD 600 in cash on Monday morning. Monday is the next business day. How are these treated for CTR purposes?
options: The Friday-night deposit counts on Monday, so the two total more than USD 10,000 on one business day and a CTR is required
They are separate days, so no CTR is required
A CTR is required only for the Friday deposit, because night and weekend deposits are reported on the calendar day they are made
A SAR is required instead of a CTR
bank.explanation: Deposits made at night, over a weekend or on a holiday are treated as received on the next business day. If the bank knows both are by the same person, they aggregate to over USD 10,000 on Monday.

bank.question: Which statement about structuring is accurate?
options: It can occur in any amount, at one or more institutions, on one or more days, if done to evade CTR reporting
It requires a single transaction over USD 10,000
It is legal if each deposit is below USD 10,000
It applies only to deposits split at a single branch on a single day, because aggregation covers one location only
bank.explanation: FinCEN defines structuring broadly: any transactions in currency, in any amount, at one or more institutions, on one or more days, in any manner, for the purpose of evading CTR requirements.

bank.question: A former Bramblecove teller was the subject of a SAR the bank filed about her conduct. Another bank now asks Bramblecove for an employment reference about her. What governs what may be shared?
options: Nothing; references are outside BSA rules
The SAR may be shared because both are banks
SAR confidentiality: nothing may reveal the SAR, though some underlying facts may be shared as the statute allows
The SAR may be shared if the former employee consents in writing, since the confidentiality rule protects the subject
bank.explanation: The rule protects the SAR and any information revealing it. It allows certain underlying facts in employment references only to the extent authorised by statute, never revealing the SAR itself.

bank.question: A compliance manager wants every 'no SAR' decision documented in a multi-page memo because 'the rule requires it'. What did the October 2025 FAQs say?
options: Every decision must be documented in full
There is no BSA requirement to document a decision not to file; a short statement usually suffices if the bank chooses to document
No documentation is ever allowed
Documentation is required only for CTRs
bank.explanation: The FAQs state there is no requirement or expectation to document a decision not to file a SAR. Banks may document under their own procedures, and a brief statement will usually suffice.

bank.question: After filing a SAR, must Bramblecove run a separate manual review of the account after 90 days to see whether the activity continued?
options: Yes; the 90-day review is a regulatory requirement
Yes, but only for business accounts
No, because once a SAR has been filed, continuing activity on the same account can never be the subject of another SAR
No; the 2025 FAQs say it may rely on risk-based monitoring instead of a separate review
bank.explanation: The FAQs confirm a separate continuing-activity review is not required. Banks may rely on reasonably designed risk-based monitoring and may follow the optional 90-day continuing-activity filing approach.

bank.question: A wire operator processes a USD 3,500 payment for a walk-in non-customer who pays in person. Which additional step does the funds transfer rule require before accepting it?
options: Filing a CTR because the amount exceeds USD 3,000
Filing a SAR for every non-customer wire
Verifying the identity of the person placing the payment order
Blocking the funds pending OFAC review
bank.explanation: For originators who are not established customers, 31 CFR 1020.410(a)(2) adds steps; where the order is made in person, the originator's bank verifies the identity of the person placing it before acceptance.

bank.question: Which pair of retention periods is correct?
options: SAR and supporting documents: five years from filing. OFAC transaction records: ten years
SAR: ten years. OFAC records: five years
SAR: three years. OFAC records: three years
SAR: five years from account closure. OFAC records: five years from the transaction, the same as other BSA records
bank.explanation: The SAR rule requires five years from filing. OFAC requires records to be kept for ten years after the transaction, or ten years after unblocking for blocked property.

bank.question: A wire to a company designated by OFAC at 9 pm is released at 7 am the next day because the vendor update had not been loaded. Which response best reflects OFAC's expectations?
options: Treat it as no violation, because the bank did not know of the designation and OFAC penalties always require knowledge or intent
Report it to FinCEN as a SAR only
Wait to see whether OFAC notices
Treat it as an apparent violation, investigate and remediate the update gap, and consider a voluntary self-disclosure
bank.explanation: OFAC can impose penalties on a strict liability basis and weighs compliance programs, remediation and self-disclosure. Bank of America's 2026 settlement included payments processed before its filter was updated.

bank.question: Under OFAC's framework, who should approve the sanctions compliance program and ensure it has adequate resources?
options: The sanctions vendor
Senior management, which may include senior executives and the board
OFAC's compliance office
The external auditor
bank.explanation: Management commitment is the first component: senior management, which typically includes senior leadership and the board, reviews and approves the program and gives it authority and resources.

bank.question: Bramblecove's sanctions training is a single module offered every two years, with no test. Measured against OFAC's framework, what is missing?
options: Approval of the module by OFAC
Training at least annually, tailored to roles, with assessments that hold employees accountable
Translation into every language
Training only for senior management
bank.explanation: OFAC's framework expects periodic training, at a minimum annually, giving job-specific knowledge, communicating responsibilities and holding employees accountable through assessments.

bank.question: Under the April 2026 proposal, how would FinCEN distinguish program failures?
options: Between large and small banks only
Between failures in anti-money laundering controls and failures in sanctions controls, which would move to OFAC supervision
Between federal and state supervisors
Between failures to establish a reasonably designed program and failures to maintain it in practice
bank.explanation: The proposal separates design deficiencies (establishment) from implementation failures (maintenance), aiming to focus action on significant or systemic failures. It was not final as of November 2026.

bank.question: Under the April 2026 proposal, what would a federal banking supervisor have to do before a significant AML/CFT supervisory action, absent urgent circumstances?
options: Give FinCEN's Director at least 30 days' advance written notice
Obtain the bank board's consent
Publish the action for public comment
Ask OFAC to review it
bank.explanation: The proposal would introduce a notice and consultation framework requiring supervisors to give FinCEN's Director at least 30 days' advance written notice before significant AML/CFT supervisory actions. It remains a proposal.

bank.question: Under the April 2026 proposal, what would a bank's risk assessment processes have to do?
options: Be approved by FinCEN before use
Be performed only every five years
Evaluate risks across products, services, channels, customers and geographies, review the AML/CFT Priorities, and be updated promptly after significant changes
Cover sanctions risk only
bank.explanation: The proposal would require risk assessment processes that evaluate ML/TF risks of business activities, review and incorporate the government's AML/CFT Priorities as appropriate, and update promptly after significant risk changes.

bank.question: What was notable about the mitigation OFAC gave Bank of America in its 2026 settlement?
options: OFAC waived the penalty entirely after self-disclosure
OFAC found the violations egregious and doubled the base penalty because the bank had not voluntarily self-disclosed them
OFAC transferred the case to FinCEN
OFAC gave no reduction to the base penalty, including none for remedial measures or cooperation
bank.explanation: OFAC said the violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed, and the settlement reflected no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remediation or cooperation.

bank.question: A mid-sized bank asks whether its BSA officer may also serve as its OFAC sanctions compliance officer. What does OFAC's framework say?
options: Never; the roles must be separate by law
One person may oversee both, depending on the bank's size and complexity
Only with OFAC's written approval
Only if the bank has no foreign customers
bank.explanation: OFAC's framework notes the sanctions compliance officer may be the same person as the BSA officer, as many institutions designate one person for financial crimes compliance, depending on size and complexity.
